issues.where: frames classic index 3-4, all-equal 3-4, one-tree 3-4, take-all 3-4, tiny-need 2-3 (beat monotonic)
issues.problem: The monotonicity demo jumps from the brute-force H (e.g. 18) to H = 10 (classic) or H = 2 (all-equal) without any narration explaining the jump; the frame before shows H = 18 and the next shows H = 10, so a student may think the algorithm skipped values arbitrarily.
issues.fix: Add one spoken line such as 'Bây giờ ta xem gỗ thay đổi thế nào khi H đổi, ví dụ ở H = 10' before the setState to frame 3, or make the demo use the H of the previous frame.

issues.where: frames classic index 5, all-equal 5, one-tree 5, take-all 5, tiny-need 4 (beat init)
issues.problem: The narration says 'lo = 0 luôn đủ gỗ vì m ≤ tổng chiều cao' but the frame's vars only contain lo, hi, m; the total height is never shown, so the claim cannot be checked on screen.
issues.fix: Add the total (e.g. sum = 62) to the frame vars or to the aux table so the invariant m ≤ tổng is visible.

issues.problem: The narration asks 'có đủ m = 7 mét gỗ không?' while the frame shows only lo, hi, mid, m; wood(mid) is not yet displayed, so the prediction is asked before the data needed to answer it is visible.
issues.fix: Either show the cut aux table (wood(mid)) in the check frame, or move the predict question to the following frame where got is shown.

issues.problem: The last three iterations are narrated without any predict question, so the interactive rhythm stops halfway; the same happens in one-tree, take-all and tiny-need.
issues.fix: Add at least one more 'check' or 'narrow' prediction in the second half of each script.

issues.problem: The pitfall is not attached to a language (no lang field) while the other two are; it is also phrased with C++-style '/', which may confuse Python readers.
issues.fix: Add lang: 'both' (or duplicate for cpp/py) and phrase it as 'làm tròn xuống (chia nguyên)'.

issues.problem: The constraint 1 ≤ m ≤ Σ h[i] is stated, but the walkthrough never mentions what happens if m = 0 or m > Σ h[i]; the code would return 0 or hi respectively without comment.
issues.fix: Add a sentence noting the guarantee m ≤ Σ h[i] is what makes lo = 0 always valid.
